title: The Active Commodity Book
subtitle: Track positions. Follow triggers. Deploy on data, not narrative.
claim: The corrected commodity book stays overweight producers, fertilizer, and gold — do not front-run a services boom that the operating data still do not support.

triggers.name: Brent Persistence
triggers.detail: One-third of SGOV first. Never the whole reserve at once.

triggers.name: Supply Loss / Kharg
triggers.detail: Split evenly. Second and final standard SGOV deployment.
triggers.context: > 13 mbpd loss or Kharg escalation = structural disruption.

triggers.name: Curve Durability
triggers.detail: Front > 20% over 6m deferred = prompt tightness, not capex recovery.
triggers.context: Backwardation above 20% means services need sustained flat curves.

triggers.name: Rig Confirmation
triggers.detail: Rigs flat/up 2 weeks. Baker Hughes Fridays. Do not force this.
triggers.context: Services valid only when rigs stop falling.

triggers.name: Fertilizer Stress
triggers.context: Hormuz handles ~30% of traded fertilizers. Already up 30-40%.

triggers.name: Gold Regime
triggers.detail: GLD > $425 or spot > $4,600. Hedge, not hero.
triggers.context: Gold driven by rates + dollar + liquidity, not just war.

triggers.name: Diesel Stress
triggers.detail: Diesel > $5.50 for 2 weeks. Transport cost transmission.

triggers.name: Shipping Stress
triggers.context: Freight costs slowing West African crude flows. Vessels stranded.

triggers.name: De-escalation
triggers.detail: Cut XOP 1/3, CF/NTR 1/4, close tankers. Rebuild VXUS + SGOV first.
triggers.context: Brent < $95 for 5 closes + restored Hormuz traffic = unwind.

rules: Review 3x/week: Monday close, Wednesday close, Friday close. Friday = Baker Hughes rig data.
Never deploy > 1/3 SGOV on one signal. Budget: $1,200/month.
No single stock > 10% of total book. No overlay > 2.5% except OIH at 5%.
No naked calls. 90-120 DTE spreads only. 2% premium cap.
De-escalation protocol: Brent < $95 for 5 closes + restored traffic → cut XOP 1/3, CF/NTR 1/4, close tankers, rebuild VXUS + SGOV.
Don't force services. Rigs falling = no OIH/HAL/SLB, even if oil is high.

fedFunds._note: Fed funds futures. Price = 100 - implied rate. ZQ=F=front month.

sections.label: Hormuz
sections.text: Strait effectively closed since Feb 28. Supply disruption: 10+ mbpd. Iran allowing selective transit for China, Russia, India, Iraq, Pakistan (Mar 26) and humanitarian/fertilizer shipments (Mar 27). U.S. military campaign to reopen since Mar 19. Trump paused energy infrastructure strikes through Apr 6. Analysts warn strait must reopen by mid-April.

sections.label: Rigs
sections.text: Baker Hughes total 543 (Mar 27), down 9 from 552. Second consecutive weekly decline. Gulf offshore at 11 rigs, down 8 YoY. SLB and HAL both guiding U.S. land activity lower for 2026.

sections.label: Fertilizer
sections.text: NOLA urea $677-690+/st. Nitrogen up 28-50%+ since conflict. CF Industries named #1 S&P 500 performer for March (UBS target raised to $140). Nutrien received Jefferies Buy upgrade ($96 target). Urea FOB US Gulf futures up 50%+ per CME Group.

sections.label: Diesel
sections.text: National average $5.375/gal (EIA, Mar 24). Up 44.6% from February ($3.72). West Coast above $6/gal.

sections.label: Fed
sections.text: Held at 3.5-3.75% (Mar 18, 11-1 vote). PCE forecast raised to 2.7%. Dot plot: 1 cut in 2026. Powell cited "substantial rise in oil prices" lifting inflation expectations.

provenance.sources: Reuters, Baker Hughes (rig count Mar 27), IEA (decline-rate study), Dallas Fed (Hormuz model Mar 20), Goldman Sachs (oil scenarios), CNBC, Federal Reserve (FOMC Mar 18), EIA (diesel Mar 24), CME Group (urea futures), DTN (fertilizer surveys), company filings (CF Industries, Nutrien, SLB, Halliburton, Transocean/Valaris). Live fetch: allorigins.win proxy to Yahoo Finance v7 spark API.
provenance.methodology: Targets are 3-6 month tactical ranges. Stops are weekly-closing (not intraday). Gap rule: if price drifts >2% from reference, targets/stops shift proportionally.
provenance.limitations: Dallas Fed model excludes gas/fertilizer disruptions. Trigger thresholds are heuristic. Monthly rebalancing assumed. Iran's selective transit policy (Mar 26) may moderate supply disruption estimates — framework does not yet model partial reopening.
provenance.disclaimer: Research framework, not financial advice. All instruments carry risk of loss.
